claims.text: The investigated alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produced by selective laser melting.
The initial SLM-produced alloy has a single-phase microstructure.
The initial alloy has a high dislocation density.
The initial alloy contains a fine dispersion of nanoscale Mn2O3 precipitates.
The nanoscale Mn2O3 precipitates are located at cell boundaries or incipient grain boundaries.
Fine Mn2O3 precipitates initially provide Orowan strengthening.
Controlled thermal aging within the service-temperature range will produce modest precipitate coarsening without conventional grain-boundary segregation.
Coarsening or redistribution of Mn2O3 precipitates increases local stress concentrations.
Coarsened precipitates impede cooperative slip and dynamic recrystallization.
The stress concentration and inhibition of slip and dynamic recrystallization cause embrittlement.
Aged samples with coarsened precipitates will have lower toughness and ductility than untreated samples.
The predicted toughness and ductility loss occurs while the alloy retains a compositionally complex single-phase microstructure.
The SLM-produced CoCrFeMnNi alloy retains comparatively high strength through approximately 700 degrees Celsius.
The alloy has a favorable strength-ductility combination from room temperature to approximately 700 degrees Celsius.
A strain rate of approximately 1 × 10^-3 s^-1 is relevant to the proposed comparison.
The proposed embrittlement transition applies up to about 700 degrees Celsius under moderate strain rates but may not apply at very low temperatures or extreme deformation rates.
Conventional-alloy toughness degradation is primarily caused by grain-boundary segregation and brittle intermetallic formation.

contradictions.description: The alloy is repeatedly described as single-phase while also being described as containing a distinct dispersion of Mn2O3 precipitates. Unless 'single-phase' is explicitly limited to the metallic matrix, these descriptions are inconsistent.
